$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Reckoning's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7R). Every ending sets climbed_the_mountain. The seal clock is set exactly once per path: scene_caravan_won (clock_steady), scene_caravan_lost (clock_late), or ending_scattered (clock_late, the lost-fight setback). Faction plays read the allies set; road callbacks read road, crossing, ember and sprites. facet_caravan is defined in gemfall-07h. Pacing episodes on the spine (Odo's barrow, the noon shake, Posy's stone, the haul vote, the last moth, the morning slide, the lookout, the downhill crowd, the last-climb vote) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Returning

plate.narration: At the Pinch, a wheelbarrow full of glitter has jammed between two rocks. Its owner looks proudly at the load. Behind him, the wagon line grows longer. Before this road can turn toward home, somebody has to get it moving.

objectives.label: Turned the Caravan Stone around for home
Talked Hessa out of her mask
Sent the wolf pack down an easier road

goal.text: Turn the road's stones toward home, and send the caravan's big stone home from the bend.

steps.label: Meet Hessa's masks on the road
Meet the big caravan at the bend

ossley_debt_stone.name: Ossley's Wet Stone
ossley_debt_stone.text: A plain river stone, always a little wet. Carry it up, and thank the river.

scene_the_pinch.narration: Every road squeezes through one gap between two red hills. The dragonlings call it the Pinch. Wagons, carts and a man with a wheelbarrow of glitter all shove through at once. At the citadel, Pellam wrote beside your names: put the stones back. So here is the plan. Turn the road's stones toward home, and send the caravan's big stone home from the bend.

scene_the_pinch_count_shakes.narration: Your dragonling counts the shakes the way the grandmothers taught, a slow breath between each. Four breaths. Then four. Then three and a half. "Grandmother says three is when you ring," your dragonling says, and stops there.

scene_glitter_barrow.narration: In the middle of the Pinch, the glitter barrow is stuck. Its owner is called Odo. His wheel is jammed between two rocks, and forty wagons behind him are shouting. "It's all gems," Odo says proudly. Most of it is painted gravel. But something in there hums.

check_glitter_barrow.prompt: Heave Odo's wheelbarrow out of the Pinch

onSuccess.narration: With a grunt and a heave, the barrow pops free and forty wagons cheer. Odo is so grateful he digs through the glitter and hands you the humming thing: a real stone, warm as a teapot. "Keeps me up at night," he says. "Singing."

onFailure.narration: You heave. The wheel pops off entirely and rolls away down the hill, and half the Pinch runs after it. In all the fuss the barrow tips, and one real stone rolls out humming at your feet. Odo waves at you to keep it. He is busy chasing a wheel.

scene_glitter_barrow_sort.narration: You tip the glitter onto a blanket. Painted gravel. Painted gravel. A button. And one real stone, warm and humming. Odo stares at his gravel a long time, then hands you the stone. "Well. Gravel doesn't sing at night, I suppose."

scene_glitter_barrow_under.narration: Your bigfoot looks under the barrow. The wheel is sitting on a glassback crab, guarding the barrow like a gem deposit. One polite tap, and the crab scuttles off, offended. Odo gives you the one real stone in his barrow.

choice_how.narration: Stones are pouring north, and you want them going home. That is a lot of stones to turn around. Who will help?

scene_wardens.narration: The wardens did just what you told them. Their checkpoint grew a gate, a ledger and a warden sergeant. Every stone goes into a numbered box. It works. A small faun watches her one shiny pebble get a number, and her lip wobbles.

scene_wardens_let_work.narration: You let the wardens work. It is quick and fair, and nobody enjoys it. The sergeant writes every number twice. The faun's pebble gets a number too. It works, you tell yourself.

scene_wardens_pebble.narration: "It's only a pebble," you say. The sergeant looks at the pebble, the box and the ledger. Then he hands it back. The faun gives you a honeycake she was saving for a very bad day.

scene_grandmothers.narration: The dragonling towns have turned gathering law inside out. A grandmother knits outside every gem-buyer's tent, saying "No, dear," until the buyer hands his stones over. One buyer is crying into a very expensive hat.

scene_grandmothers_queue.narration: You keep the line of sorry buyers moving. One tries to sneak off without handing anything over. Three grandmothers say "No, dear" at once, in harmony. He comes back and empties both pockets.

scene_grandmothers_knit.narration: A grandmother hands you needles and wool. By noon you knit badly, and two buyers have handed over their sacks rather than watch you drop another stitch. "That's the trick," says the grandmother. "Nobody can stand it."

check_handcart.prompt: Talk travelers into letting their stones go home

onSuccess.narration: A handcart, a sign that says STONES GOING HOME, and a lot of honest talking. By lunchtime the cart is half full, and somebody has drawn a smiley face on the sign.

onFailure.narration: Most people walk straight past the sign. One man gives you a stone, asks for it back, then gives it again. The cart is nearly empty, but at least you know which wagons hum the loudest.

scene_noon_shake.narration: At noon the ground gives a big shrug. A sack splits, and its stones roll out. Not downhill. Uphill, all together, like ducklings after their mother. A warden drops his pencil.

variants.text: None of the runaways are yours.
Your great stones tug at their straps, wanting to follow.
Your great stones strain so hard you have to sit on a pack.

check_noon_shake.prompt: Scoop up a sack of stones that are rolling the wrong way

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and juggle. Every last stone ends up in your arms, still humming, still leaning gently uphill, like puppies pulling on a lead.

onFailure.narration: The stones slip through your fingers and roll straight into a goat pen. The goat gives them back one at a time, very slowly, and wants a scratch behind the ears for every single one.

scene_noon_shake_follow.narration: You follow them up the road. They stop at the last red rock in a neat line, all pointing straight at Mount Red Sky. You pick them up gently. They seem a little disappointed.

scene_noon_shake_harvest.narration: You hold up the Harvest Stone, and the rolling stones change their minds. One by one they roll to your feet instead and hum along with it. The warden picks up his pencil and writes that down.

scene_road_gifts.narration: A warden runner brings a note from Pellam's ledger: your names, and RETURN. Under it, very small: HOW IS IT GOING? Then the road starts bringing back things you did on the way here, as if the realm kept your receipts.

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat poles a flat boat up a dry creek: OLD OSSLEY, the frog from the reeds of the Great River. His boat is full of stones the river took. "Stones want to go home," he says. "We only kept them until someone was going that way."

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley's price was never coin. He presses one plain, wet stone into your hand. "Carry this one up yourself. When you put it down, say thank you to the river."

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with moss in her hair and grumbling mules. She counts your cord's knots. "Knot, knot, knot. Good!" Then she unloads what the Woods took from careless hunters: shovels, a teapot, one very surprised hat, and lots of stones.

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel of scribbled paper sidles up, not looking at you. "Catalog," it tells nobody. "Who bought what in the marsh. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

scene_boggart_grandma_said.narration: You repeat what Grandmother Tull said about the bell nobody rings, even the part she said twice. The boggart closes its eyes to listen. "Lovely," it tells nobody, and lets go of the catalog.

scene_boggart_wardens_said.narration: "It hums!" you shout in Dunmore's exact voice. The boggart shivers with joy and writes it down twice, once backwards. "That's a keeper." It hands over the catalog, still not looking at you.

scene_ford_witch.narration: It is Mother Thrum, the witch from the ford, with a ringing wool sock under one arm. She walked the whole road north. "I always ask twice," she says. "Once at the ford, once at the mountain. What do you actually want?"

scene_ford_witch_not_sure.narration: Mother Thrum nods slowly, as if that beats most answers. She keeps her ringing sock, and gives you a songbird ribbon instead, "for the working out." She will ask again. She always does.

scene_ford_witch_put_back.narration: Mother Thrum looks at you over her glasses. Then she sets a stone from the ford in your hands. For the first time, it stops ringing. "That was the answer," she says. "Took you long enough."

scene_posy.narration: Up the road comes a tired prospector called Corbin, with his daughter Posy on his shoulders. They spent everything to get here. Posy holds a small humming stone in both fists. "It's my lucky one," she says. "It's going to make us rich." Corbin looks at your stones going home and says nothing.

check_posy.prompt: Help a little girl decide to give up her lucky stone

onSuccess.narration: You tell Posy about the mountain and the hum, the gentle version. She thinks about it very hard. Then she opens her fists and puts the stone on your pile herself. "So it can go home," she says. Corbin lets out a breath he has been holding since spring.

onFailure.narration: Posy listens, and then hides the stone behind her back. "It's mine," she says, and her lip wobbles. You do not push. Corbin gives you a small, sorry nod, and the two of them go on up the road toward the camps.

scene_posy_let_keep.narration: You wish them luck, and mean it. Posy waves her stone as they go, humming all the way around the corner. Maybe the mountain will not mind one small stone a little longer.

scene_posy_medal.narration: You show Posy the sprites' tiny medal that says NOT. "You got a medal for not taking something?" She looks at her stone, then the medal. Then she puts the stone on your pile, and asks if sprites give medals to girls.

scene_masks.narration: Down the road, people in bark masks are working the funnel backwards. They are Hessa's friends from the soup tent, the Deep Hollow. They want to wake the mountain so it can fix things, so they collect stones from anyone who will give. "We'll break the seal properly," says one. You know that voice. It is Hessa herself.

scene_masks_let_be.narration: You let them be, and work your own side of the road. You pass stones in opposite directions, ten steps apart, like a very slow dance. Once Hessa looks up and nods. You nod back.

scene_masks_mask_swap.narration: Your kitsune borrows a mask from a cart hook and strolls into the masks' camp, humming along. Soon your kitsune strolls back out with a sack of stones "for the break" and a bowl of very good soup.

check_tamsin.prompt: Convince Hessa the seal is not a cage

onSuccess.narration: Hessa takes off her mask. "I only wanted somebody to fix things," she says quietly. She hands you her whole sack of stones, and then her ladle, and asks you to fix things.

onFailure.narration: She listens kindly, all the way to the end. Then she puts her mask back on. "I hope you're right," she says. "I don't think you are." Her cell rolls on with a full sack.

choice_haul.narration: Your pile of going-home stones now fills a borrowed cart, far too heavy to push. It must get up the hill to the dragonling way-shelter before dark, where it will be safe. The ground shrugs, as if to say hurry. How will you move it?

variants.text: None of it is yours. Strangers trusted you with all of it.
A few of your own great stones ride on top, humming.
Your own great stones tug uphill like eager dogs.

check_haul_goat.prompt: Make friends with a grumpy snowhorn goat

onSuccess.narration: The goat sniffs you, sniffs the cart, and decides you are acceptable. It pulls the whole load up the hill at a steady trot, stopping only once, to eat the corner of your sign.

onFailure.narration: The goat sits down. It will not move. In the end you pull the cart on your own, and the goat rides on top of the stones, looking very pleased with itself, all the way to the shelter.

check_haul_carry.prompt: Carry the whole pile up the hill, sack by sack

onSuccess.narration: You make a chain up the hill and pass the sacks along, hand to hand, singing a counting song. Strangers on the road join in. By the top the chain is forty people long, and nobody remembers who started it.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up, your arms turn to noodles. You sit down on the sacks to rest, and a passing grandmother tuts, hitches your cart to her own wagon, and tows the lot up the hill without a word.

check_haul_sledge.prompt: Build a sled that slides uphill

onSuccess.narration: Rope, a broken door and some greased planks. The sled glides up the slope on its runners like a dream, and a crowd of dragonling children follow it all the way to the shelter, asking for a turn.

onFailure.narration: The sled works beautifully, in the wrong direction. It slides gently back to the bottom of the hill twice before you think to tie it to a tree and winch it up, one heave at a time. It gets there. Eventually.

choice_haul_others.narration: Your own arms are empty, so you fill them with everybody else's. Travelers hand you their sacks. You climb, set one down in the shelter yard, and climb down for another. By dusk the yard is full.

scene_evening.narration: Evening. The going-home stones sit safe in the shelter yard, humming. Below, campfires pop up along the road like beads on a string.

variants.text: None of them are yours, but they hum just as loudly.
A few of your own great stones hum among them.
Your own great stones hum loudest of all.

scene_evening_campfire.narration: You join a campfire with a faun family, a warden off duty, and a prospector with one boot. The prospector says the shaking is nothing. The warden says nothing, which is worse. The faun children make you tell the funny bit twice.

scene_relay_sing.narration: The centaur relay singers at the campfires sing about wagons that have not come yet. A grandmother's runner hands you a list of caves nobody may ever dig. It is exactly where you would put a seal.

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings!" cries Madame Coralie Fenn from her barrel on wheels, tied to a caravan roof. She has the warm red stone you sold her on the quay, your very first. Now it sits in a velvet box, and its price has gone way up.

scene_ember_wave.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms, and her barrel wobbles. "Next time, darlings!" The caravan rolls on, with your very first stone humming on top.

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay. Madame Fenn hugs the velvet box before handing it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings." The stone is warm as toast, and it hums as if it remembers you.

scene_last_moth.narration: At the shelter door, something small bumps the lantern. Tap. Tap. It is an embermoth, glowing like a coal, the first you have seen all day. The others flew south. This one is going the wrong way, and it looks very tired.

scene_last_moth_lantern.narration: You open the lantern door. The moth crawls in and settles beside the wick, glowing a bit brighter. The shelter cat watches it all night without blinking once.

scene_last_moth_south.narration: You carry it to the south wall and open your hands. The moth drifts away down the valley after the others, a tiny spark getting smaller. It is the right way. It still feels lonely to watch.

scene_last_moth_feel.narration: Your unicorn touches the moth with the tip of the horn. "It isn't lost," your unicorn says. "It's homesick. It wants to go up, but not alone." The moth climbs into your unicorn's mane and glows there all night.

rest_way_shelter.narration: The way-shelter's bell is tied up with ribbon, so nobody rings it by accident. There is soup, a cat, and a wall of children's drawings of the mountain. Patch up your scrapes. Tomorrow is the worst bend.

scene_morning_slide.narration: In the night, half a hillside slid onto the road. A heap of red rocks taller than a wagon blocks it. A warden writes ROAD CLOSED on his clipboard in very small letters, as if that will help.

check_morning_slide.prompt: Find the one rock that holds up all the others, and pull

onSuccess.narration: You find the one rock that holds up all the rest, and pull. The whole heap shrugs, sighs, and slides politely off the edge of the road. The warden crosses out CLOSED and writes OPEN, in slightly bigger letters.

onFailure.narration: The big rock will not budge. But behind it, between two boulders, there is a gap just wide enough to wriggle through. You come out the other side red with dust from head to toe, and the warden writes that down too.

scene_morning_slide_goat_path.narration: A goat path runs above the slide, about as wide as a sandwich. You go single file, not looking down. A snowhorn goat coming the other way steps politely aside onto what looks like nothing at all.

scene_morning_slide_verses.narration: You sing the Spiral Verses from the rush road, in order, the way the relay taught. One verse is about this very hill: an old cart track that curls around the back. And there it is, behind the gorse.

scene_morning_slide_reed_knot.narration: Ossley's reed knot, which never dries, starts dripping sideways. You follow the drips to a dry stream bed that runs under the slide through a tunnel of old roots. Ossley would say nothing about this. You say nothing either.

scene_switchback.narration: The road zigzags up toward the worst bend. Coming down it the wrong way is a pack of cinder wolves. They are not hunting. They are leaving the mountain, and you are in their way.

scene_switchback_fly_round.narration: You fly up and find a side path the wolves missed. You lead everyone along it, one careful step at a time. Below, the pack streams down the road like a long gray ribbon.

scene_switchback_sprite_knots.narration: Tiny knots of grass, tied at ankle height, lead along a goat path above the zigzags. The harvest sprites are still looking out for you this far north. The wolves pour past below without looking up.

check_wolves.prompt: Roll a smoked sausage down the side trail at exactly the right moment

onSuccess.narration: The sausage bounces down the side trail, and the whole pack follows it with enormous dignity, as if that was where they were going all along.

onFailure.narration: The sausage bounces off a rock and lands right back at your feet. The wolves look at the sausage. Then they look at you.

encounter_wolves.narration: The pack spreads across the zigzags, ears flat, too scared to think straight.

onVictory.narration: The pack decides you are more trouble than you are worth, and pours past you.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves bowl through you. Nobody is hurt, but the cart tips, and the stones roll every which way.

scene_bend_lookout.narration: The caravan is still below the bend, so you have a little time to get ready. A big sign could ask the caravan master to stop. A scout could pick out the humming wagon. The ground hums under your boots.

check_bend_scout.prompt: Sneak along the ridge and pick out the humming wagon

onSuccess.narration: You creep along the ridge and watch. Mules with cotton in their ears. A caravan master rubbing her head every few minutes, as if it aches. And the middle wagon, humming so hard its canvas trembles. You know exactly where to go now.

onFailure.narration: You creep along the ridge, slip on loose gravel, and slide most of the way down to the road on your bottom. A mule looks at you. You look at the mule. Neither of you tells anybody, and you scramble back up just in time.

scene_bend_lookout_sign.narration: You paint STONES GOING HOME on an old tent, in letters as tall as a goat, and stretch it between two rocks. It is a bit wonky. One S is backwards. It is the biggest sign on the mountain.

scene_bend_lookout_table_stone.narration: You hold up the Table Stone, and from far below, the middle wagon answers. Two stones hum to each other across the valley, like two cows calling over a field. Now you know which wagon it is.

choice_the_bend.narration: The worst bend is a hairpin over a long drop, where every wagon must slow down. Here comes the fattest caravan, twelve wagons long. In the middle wagon, something hums so loudly the mules have cotton in their ears.

choice_the_bend_heard_it.narration: You heard this caravan in last night's song, so you reach the bend an hour early. You are already sitting on the rock where the lead wagon must stop. The caravan master looks at you as if you cheated, which, in a way, you did.

choice_the_bend_relay.narration: You whistle toward the relay road. A centaur appears on the ridge, two more behind her. Together they steer the caravan off the main road and right up to you, as neat as threading a needle.

check_caravan_helped.prompt: Ask the caravan master to send the humming stone home, with help at your back

onSuccess.narration: The caravan master looks at you, at the help behind you, at the shaking ground, and sighs a sigh that goes all the way down to her boots. "Fine. Take it. It's been giving me headaches."

onFailure.narration: She almost says yes. Then the ground lurches, the mules bolt, and in the muddle a masked wagoneer steers the middle wagon off up a side track.

check_caravan.prompt: Convince a tired caravan master to give up the best stone she has ever carried

onSuccess.narration: You tell her the whole truth, from the humming to the seal. She is quiet for a long time. Then she climbs into the middle wagon and comes back holding the stone in both hands.

onFailure.narration: She has heard a lot of stories this season. She does not believe yours. While you are still arguing, a masked wagoneer quietly steers the middle wagon off up a side track.

scene_caravan_won.narration: The caravan's great stone, called the Caravan Stone, is the size of a loaf of bread and hums like a whole choir. The moment it points back up the mountain, its hum changes key. It sounds faintly relieved. The next tremor is a little softer.

scene_caravan_lost.narration: The masks have the humming stone. They drive it away up the side track, and one of them waves to you, sorry. Behind them the ground stops shrugging and starts shaking, slow and steady, like a drum.

scene_downhill_crowd.narration: Higher up, the whole road is coming down: wagons, wardens, a faun family with their chairs tied to a mule. Beside you, the fauns' little cart drops a wheel into a crack and sticks fast. The smallest faun starts to cry.

check_downhill_cart.prompt: Heave a faun cart out of a crack in the road

onSuccess.narration: One, two, three, heave! The wheel pops out of the crack and the cart rolls on. The fauns shout thank you all the way down the hill, and the smallest one throws you a very squashed flower.

onFailure.narration: Heave as you might, the wheel stays stuck. So you lift the whole cart out instead, which takes everybody, the mule and a passing warden. The fauns say thank you seven times each.

scene_downhill_crowd_unload.narration: You carry everything across the crack: six chairs, a cooking pot, an empty birdcage, and the smallest faun, who stops crying to ride on your shoulders. Empty, the cart lifts out easily. You wave them off down the hill.

scene_downhill_crowd_posy.narration: It is Posy, running up while everyone runs down, with Corbin puffing behind. She pushes her lucky stone into your hand. "It kept humming at night. I think it was asking. You take it home." Corbin pops the faun cart free.

scene_downhill_crowd_odo.narration: Odo clatters down with his empty wheelbarrow, just the right size for six chairs and a small faun. Odo wheels them all around the crack, singing. "Never carried anything worth this much," he says. He means the fauns.

choice_last_climb.narration: Above the last houses, the road splits. Left, a warden stair cut straight up the rock, steep and quick. Right, the old dragonling path, which wanders and takes its time. Behind you, the ground shakes in a slow, steady beat. Which way up?

check_last_climb_stair.prompt: Race up a steep stair before the light goes

onSuccess.narration: Up and up and up, two steps at a time. You reach the top with your legs wobbling and your heart thumping, well ahead of the dark.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up, a tremor shakes loose a shower of little stones. You press flat against the rock and wait, and then climb on carefully, one step at a time, and reach the top dusty but whole, just as the light turns orange.

choice_last_climb_old_path.narration: The old path wanders, but it is kind. It finds shade and a cold spring. At every bend, a carved dragonling face smiles at you. You count eleven. By the twelfth, nobody's legs hurt at all.

choice_last_climb_moth.narration: The little embermoth flies ahead along a ledge nobody else noticed. It glows at every turn so you can follow. At the tree line it circles you once, like a thank you, and flies on toward home.

rest_tree_line.narration: At the tree line, you look back. Everyone else is running downhill, even a man with an empty wheelbarrow. You turn and climb, arms full of stones that want to go home.

variants.text: At the tree line, you look back. Everyone else is running downhill, even a man with an empty wheelbarrow. You turn and climb, hands empty and packs humming, to see what you can still do.
Every great stone you carry hums all the way up.

ending_scattered.narration: By the time you find half the stones, the caravan has passed the bend without you. The ground shakes in a slow, patient rhythm. You pick up what you can carry and climb anyway, far behind.

scene_quiet_work.narration: You tell nobody what you are for. You just start. A stone slipped from a sack here, a pocket emptied there. Nobody notices, which is the point. By noon, the pile behind your tent is humming.

interaction_stone_chain.narration: You help the warden pack the runaway stones into sacks, away from the wagon wheels. He counts the last one and pays you three coins. "Honest work," he says. Then, quietly, "I have never been so glad to be bored."

interaction_shelter_stack.narration: At the way-shelter, a keeper named Brindle helps you settle the stones on a board as big as a door. Then she tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "From my own pot," she says. "Don't tell the cat."

scene_evening_cakes.narration: You count two coins into Brindle's floury palm. She hands you a bag of warm honeycakes, and a look that says she knows how many you will eat before breakfast.

interaction_trickle.narration: Past the slide, small red stones trickle across the road in bursts. Ping, ping, ping. Then they stop. "Go in the gaps!" calls the warden.

interaction.cue: Wait for the pebbles to stop, then tap to dash across.

onSuccess.narration: You dash across in the quiet. The pebbles patter behind you.

onFailure.narration: Ping! A pebble bonks your hat. You run the rest of the way, laughing. Nobody is hurt. The warden writes down "bonked."

onAssisted.narration: The warden calls out each gap, and you slip across without a single bonk.

interaction_wagon_bells.narration: The caravan comes around the hairpin, bells ringing. In front is the caravan master, a tired woman with a headache. She rings a tune to the wagons behind: low bell, high bell, low bell, brass bell. It means "slow down, make room." Ring it back, and she will stop to hear you.

interaction.cue: Listen to the bells, then ring them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: The master hears her own tune come back, blinks, and holds up one hand. The whole caravan eases to a stop.

onFailure.narration: Your tune comes out wrong. The lead mule winces. "Is that a bell?" asks the master, slowing anyway. "It's the saddest bell I've ever heard."

onAssisted.narration: A wagoneer rings the tune again, slowly, until you have it. The master hears it ring back, and the caravan eases to a stop.

scene_drake_ledge.narration: Where the paths meet, a little spring bubbles out of the rock. A young river drake, long as a rowboat, lies across the path in front of it. Its creek dried up in the shaking, so it climbed here for water. It thinks everybody wants its spring, and it will not let anyone near.

encounter_drake.narration: The drake hisses like a kettle and lashes its tail. It does not want to hurt anybody. It only wants the spring. Drive it back from the path, and give it room to drink.

scene_drake_drinks.narration: The drake backs off and plunges its snout into the spring. Gulp, gulp, gulp. The splash wakes a sunbloom, which opens at once. You fill a flask with spring water and one gold petal.

scene_drake_rescued.narration: The drake's tail sweeps your feet out, and everyone sits down hard in the moss. Nobody is hurt. A warden runner empties a water-skin over the drake's snout, and it goes off to sulk in the spring. No flask tonight, but the path is clear.

interaction_haul_team.narration: The sacks keep leaning uphill. Odo brings a plank with THIS WAY UP painted on both ends. Brace the load together.

interaction.cue: Hold the sacks steady while the load is moved.

onSuccess.narration: Not one sack runs away. The plank points both ways, but you do not.

onFailure.narration: The shelter keeper steadies the load. The sacks arrive safely.

onAssisted.narration: The shelter keeper braces the other side. Together you carry the load uphill.

interaction_return_handover.narration: The master turns into the lay-by. She will send the Caravan Stone home if you hold the wagon steady while she unloads. The mules start their lunch.

interaction.cue: Brace the wagon while the master unloads the stone.

onSuccess.narration: The stone is safe in your arms. "Home delivery," says the master, pointing uphill.

onFailure.narration: A driver steadies the wheel. Together you finish the handover.

onAssisted.narration: The master brings a wheel block. Together you unload the stone.

scene_sign_agreement.narration: The caravan master reads your enormous sign and nods. She will stop in the lay-by so you can send the stone home. One mule tries to eat the sign.

scene_wagon_agreement.narration: You meet the marked wagon right where it stops. The master hears her bell call again and agrees to unload in the lay-by. No shouting over twelve wagons.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, urgent, a little spooky but never scary; the realm sending back what the party gave it

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow cell member who ran the soup tent; gentle, sad, sure she is helping; says 'properly' a lot
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.warden_sergeant: rigid, honest, tired; counts everything; secretly hates making children cry
npcVoices.grandmother: dragonling gatherer; knits while she talks; 'No, dear' is a complete sentence
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, has had a headache since the stone came aboard
npcVoices.odo: a cheerful man with a wheelbarrow of painted gravel he believes is gems; proud, easily delighted, never sulks
npcVoices.posy: Corbin the prospector's small daughter; serious, brave, thinks hard before she answers

interaction_stone_chain.narration: The warden who dropped his pencil has found another one, and a plan. He lines everybody up along the road, and the runaway stones are to go hand to hand, away from the wheels, into his sacks. "Pass them back and do not drop any!" he calls. "There is a little pay in it for the people in this line."

interaction.cue: Catch the stone, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The last stone drops into the last sack, and the warden writes a very tidy number in his ledger. He counts three coins into your hands. "Honest work," he says, and then, quieter, "I have never been so glad to be bored."

onFailure.narration: One stone slips through and rolls off uphill to join its friends. The warden writes it down sadly. The rest are safe in the sacks, and the line cheers anyway.

onAssisted.narration: The warden joins the line himself, and together you pass the stones along without losing a single one. He counts three coins into your hands. "Honest work," he says.

interaction_shelter_stack.narration: At the dragonling way-shelter, the keeper meets your pile at the gate. Her name is Brindle, and she is carrying a board as big as a door. "Stack them on here, then carry the board up to the top shelf," she says. "Level, mind. Stones hum louder when they tilt, and then nobody sleeps." She wants every one of them safe before the next shrug.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the stones sit level, then carry the board.

onSuccess.narration: The stones sit as still as eggs. Brindle taps the shelf twice, satisfied, and tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "From my own pot," she says. "Do not tell the cat."

onFailure.narration: The board tips and the stones hum like angry bees. Brindle lays one hand on the loudest of them, and it quiets down at once, embarrassed. "Wobbly day," she says. "Up they go."

onAssisted.narration: Brindle takes one corner of the board herself, and the stones sit as still as eggs. She tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "From my own pot," she says. "Do not tell the cat."
